questions.q: What compound interest is earned on ₹10,000 at 10% per annum for one year when interest is compounded half-yearly?
questions.e: Half-yearly compounding divides the annual rate into two periods. The rate per half-year is 10% ÷ 2 = 5%, and there are two periods. Amount = 10,000 × 1.05 × 1.05 = ₹11,025. Compound interest = 11,025 − 10,000 = ₹1,025.

questions.q: A vehicle travels the same distance at 40 km/h and 60 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances, average speed is not the simple arithmetic mean. Let each distance be d. Total distance is 2d and total time is d/40 + d/60 = d/24. Therefore average speed = 2d ÷ (d/24) = 48 km/h. The harmonic-mean formula gives the same result: 2ab/(a+b).

questions.q: A can finish a job alone in 12 days and B in 18 days. They work on alternate days, beginning with A. How long will the job take?
questions.e: In two days, A and B together complete 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36 of the job. Six two-day cycles complete 30/36 = 5/6 in 12 days. On day 13, A adds 1/12 = 3/36, so 33/36 is complete. On day 14, B adds 1/18 = 2/36, so 35/36 is complete and 1/36 remains. A completes that fraction in (1/36) ÷ (1/12) = 1/3 day. Total time is 14⅓ days.

questions.q: A bag contains 5 red balls and 3 blue balls. Two balls are drawn one after another without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?

questions.q: A two-digit number has digits whose sum is 11. The tens digit is 3 greater than the units digit. What is the number?

Meeting of warm and cold ocean currents
Descent of dry air over subtropical high-pressure belts

A layer of permanently frozen groundwater
questions.e: The O horizon is the surface organic layer containing leaf litter and decomposing organic matter. Below it, the A horizon is commonly mineral topsoil mixed with humus, while the B horizon often receives materials leached from upper layers. Recognising the horizons helps interpret soil development.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography

questions.q: A Mercator map is useful for navigation because it preserves local angles and directions, but what important distortion increases towards the poles?
o: The equator is shown as a point
Distances along every route become exact
questions.e: The Mercator projection is conformal: it preserves local angles and makes constant-bearing routes appear as straight lines. However, its scale increases with latitude, greatly enlarging areas near the poles. Greenland therefore appears much larger relative to equatorial regions than its true area warrants.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography

questions.q: The term 'doldrums' traditionally refers to the:
o: Subtropical belt of descending dry air
Equatorial low-pressure belt with weak and variable surface winds
questions.e: The doldrums are associated with the equatorial low-pressure belt, where intense heating causes air to rise and surface winds may be weak or variable. The region is also associated with the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone. It is different from the subtropical high-pressure belts, often called horse latitudes.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography

questions.q: Other factors being comparable, why do inland locations often experience a larger annual temperature range than coastal locations?
o: Land heats and cools more rapidly than the sea
Land has a higher specific heat capacity than water
Ocean currents stop all seasonal temperature change
Coastal air contains no water vapour
questions.e: Land generally heats and cools more rapidly than water. The sea moderates nearby temperatures because water has a higher specific heat capacity and ocean mixing distributes heat. Far inland, this maritime influence weakens, so summers may be hotter and winters colder, producing a larger annual temperature range.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography

questions.q: A deep, narrow coastal inlet with steep sides, formed when a glacially carved valley is flooded by seawater, is called a:
o: A deep, narrow glacial valley flooded by seawater
A river island formed by deposition
A limestone cave with underground streams
questions.e: A fjord is a deep, narrow inlet formed when a glacially carved valley is flooded by the sea. Its steep sides reflect the erosional work of a glacier. Fjords are common along formerly glaciated high-latitude coasts, especially in Norway and parts of New Zealand and Chile.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography

questions.q: At the level of a producing unit, Gross Value Added (GVA) is calculated as:
o: Value of output minus intermediate consumption
Value of output plus intermediate consumption
Gross fixed capital formation minus depreciation
questions.e: GVA measures the value created by a producer. It is calculated as the value of output minus the value of intermediate goods and services consumed in production. This prevents the same intermediate input from being counted again at each stage of the production chain.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Statistics for Economics.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Statistics for Economics

questions.q: A government has a fiscal deficit of ₹8 lakh crore and pays ₹3 lakh crore as interest on past debt. What is its primary deficit?
questions.e: Primary deficit equals fiscal deficit minus interest payments. Therefore ₹8 lakh crore − ₹3 lakh crore = ₹5 lakh crore. The measure shows the current borrowing requirement after excluding interest payments arising from accumulated past debt.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Union Budget — Budget at a Glance and fiscal indicators.
questions.sourceName: Union Budget — Budget at a Glance and fiscal indicators

questions.q: Which government expenditure is most clearly classified as capital expenditure?
o: Payment of monthly salaries to staff
Construction of a new public bridge
questions.e: Capital expenditure generally creates assets or reduces liabilities. Building a public bridge creates a durable public asset, so it is capital expenditure. Salaries, stationery and electricity bills are ordinarily revenue expenditure because they meet recurring operating costs rather than directly creating a new asset.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Union Budget — Budget at a Glance and expenditure classification.
questions.sourceName: Union Budget — Budget at a Glance and expenditure classification

questions.q: Proceeds received by the Union Government from selling part of its equity holding in a public sector enterprise are ordinarily classified as:
questions.e: Disinvestment proceeds are classified as non-debt capital receipts. They provide funds through the sale of government assets or equity holdings and do not create a repayment obligation in the way borrowings do. They are therefore distinct from both tax revenue and debt-creating receipts.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Union Budget — Receipts Budget.
questions.sourceName: Union Budget — Receipts Budget

questions.q: In a simplified economy, a sharp increase in government borrowing may raise interest rates and reduce private investment. This effect is known as:
questions.e: The crowding-out effect describes how increased government borrowing may put upward pressure on interest rates or absorb available loanable funds, leaving less finance for private investment. The strength of the effect depends on economic conditions, monetary policy and the availability of savings; it is not inevitable in every situation.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics and public finance concepts.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics and public finance concepts

questions.q: Which example best illustrates an automatic stabiliser in a modern tax-and-transfer system?
o: Parliament votes on a new road project every month
Income-tax collections fall automatically when taxable incomes decline during a downturn
The central bank announces a new policy rate after every election
A government sells a public enterprise to finance a festival
questions.e: An automatic stabiliser changes government revenue or expenditure without a new discretionary policy decision. When incomes fall, progressive income-tax collections usually decline automatically, cushioning disposable income. Some transfer payments may also rise as eligibility increases. This helps moderate economic fluctuations.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics and public finance concepts.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics and public finance concepts

questions.q: If an export price index is 120 and an import price index is 100, what is the terms-of-trade index using export prices divided by import prices and multiplied by 100?
questions.e: The terms-of-trade index is (export price index ÷ import price index) × 100. Substituting the values gives (120 ÷ 100) × 100 = 120. A rise in this index means export prices have increased relative to import prices, other things being equal.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics and international trade concepts.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics and international trade concepts

questions.q: In a simple Keynesian model, if the marginal propensity to consume is 0.8 and there are no taxes or imports, what is the simple expenditure multiplier?
questions.e: The simple multiplier is 1/(1−MPC). With MPC = 0.8, the multiplier is 1/0.2 = 5. An initial increase in autonomous expenditure can therefore produce a larger total change in equilibrium income as the spending circulates through successive rounds. The result assumes the simplified model stated in the question.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics

questions.q: Which of the following is ordinarily revenue expenditure rather than capital expenditure for a government department?
o: Construction of a new hospital building
Routine annual maintenance of office equipment
Acquisition of land for a public project
questions.e: Routine annual maintenance of office equipment is generally revenue expenditure because it meets recurring operating costs and does not normally create a new asset. Construction of a hospital, a bridge or acquisition of land for a public project is ordinarily treated as capital expenditure under government budget classification.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Union Budget — Budget at a Glance and expenditure classification.
questions.sourceName: Union Budget — Budget at a Glance and expenditure classification

questions.q: Which cells are the principal source of insulin in the human pancreas?
o: Alpha cells of the islets of Langerhans
Beta cells of the islets of Langerhans
Delta cells of the islets of Langerhans
questions.e: Insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the pancreatic islets of Langerhans. It helps lower blood glucose by promoting glucose uptake and storage in responsive tissues. Alpha cells mainly secrete glucagon, which raises blood glucose. The distinction is important in understanding endocrine regulation of metabolism.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Biology textbooks.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Science and Biology textbooks

questions.q: In the human respiratory system, the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide between air and blood occurs mainly across the walls of the:
questions.e: Alveoli are tiny air sacs surrounded by dense networks of capillaries. Their thin, moist walls and large combined surface area allow oxygen to diffuse into the blood and carbon dioxide to diffuse from the blood into the alveolar air. The trachea and bronchi mainly conduct air.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Biology textbooks.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Science and Biology textbooks

questions.q: The oxygen-carrying capacity of red blood cells depends mainly on haemoglobin, whose oxygen-binding component contains which element?
questions.e: Haemoglobin contains heme groups with iron at their centre. Oxygen binds reversibly to the iron-containing heme, allowing red blood cells to transport oxygen from the lungs to body tissues. Iron deficiency can reduce haemoglobin production and contribute to anaemia.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Biology textbooks.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Science and Biology textbooks

questions.q: In terms of electron transfer, oxidation is defined as:
o: Loss of protons from the nucleus
questions.e: Oxidation is loss of electrons, while reduction is gain of electrons. The two processes occur together in a redox reaction because electrons lost by one species are gained by another. The mnemonic OIL RIG—Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain—helps remember the definitions.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Chemistry textbooks.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Science and Chemistry textbooks

questions.q: At the same temperature, a solution of pH 3 has how many times the hydrogen-ion concentration of a solution of pH 5?
questions.e: The pH scale is logarithmic: a decrease of one pH unit represents a tenfold increase in hydrogen-ion concentration. A difference of two units therefore represents 10 × 10 = 100 times. Thus the pH 3 solution has 100 times the hydrogen-ion concentration of the pH 5 solution.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Chemistry textbooks.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Science and Chemistry textbooks

questions.q: When pure ice at its melting point changes into liquid water at the same temperature, the heat absorbed is called:
questions.e: Latent heat of fusion is the heat required to change a unit mass of a substance from solid to liquid at its melting point without a change in temperature. The supplied energy changes the state by overcoming intermolecular forces rather than raising the temperature.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Physics textbooks.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Science and Physics textbooks

questions.q: When a swimmer pushes water backward and moves forward, which law best explains the forward motion?
o: Law of conservation of electric charge
questions.e: Newton's third law states that for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. The swimmer pushes water backward; the water exerts an equal and opposite force on the swimmer, pushing the swimmer forward. The action and reaction forces act on different bodies, so they do not cancel each other on one body.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Physics textbooks.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Science and Physics textbooks

questions.q: A force of 100 newtons acts normally on an area of 0.5 square metre. What pressure is produced?
questions.e: Pressure is force divided by the area over which it acts: P = F/A. Here P = 100 ÷ 0.5 = 200 pascals. For the same force, reducing the contact area increases pressure; this explains why a sharp blade cuts more easily than a blunt one.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Physics textbooks.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Science and Physics textbooks

questions.q: In a chemical reaction carried out in a sealed container, which statement expresses the law of conservation of mass?
o: The mass of products is always greater than reactants
The total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products
Mass disappears when a gas is formed
Only the mass of solid substances is conserved
questions.e: The law of conservation of mass states that matter is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction. In a closed system, the total mass before reaction equals the total mass after reaction. If a gas escapes from an open vessel, the measured mass may appear to decrease, but the total matter is still conserved.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Chemistry textbooks.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Science and Chemistry textbooks

questions.q: In the modern periodic table, a vertical column is called a:
questions.e: A vertical column in the modern periodic table is a group, while a horizontal row is a period. Elements in the same group often show similar chemical properties because of related valence-electron configurations. The terms should not be interchanged when reading periodic trends.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Chemistry textbooks.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Science and Chemistry textbooks

questions.q: A high five-day Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) reading in a river sample most directly indicates:
o: A large amount of oxygen is being used by microorganisms to break down organic matter
The water contains no dissolved salts
The water is necessarily free from pathogens
questions.e: BOD measures the oxygen consumed by microorganisms while decomposing biodegradable organic matter under specified test conditions. A high BOD generally indicates a heavier organic pollution load and can reduce dissolved oxygen available to aquatic organisms. It is not a direct test for salinity or pathogen absence.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Central Pollution Control Board — Water Quality Criteria.
questions.sourceName: Central Pollution Control Board — Water Quality Criteria

questions.q: Which pair of gases is the principal precursor of human-caused acid deposition?
questions.e: Sulphur dioxide (SO₂) and nitrogen oxides (NOₓ) are emitted largely from fossil-fuel combustion. They react in the atmosphere with water, oxygen and other chemicals to form sulphuric and nitric acids, which return to Earth through wet or dry deposition. The resulting acidity can affect soils, forests and water bodies.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. US Environmental Protection Agency — What Is Acid Rain?.
questions.sourceName: US Environmental Protection Agency — What Is Acid Rain?

questions.q: In ecology, the carrying capacity of a habitat refers to:
o: The maximum population it can support over time under prevailing conditions
The total number of species ever recorded in the habitat
The speed at which a predator catches prey
The number of trophic levels in a food chain
questions.e: Carrying capacity is the population size that an environment can sustain over time with its available food, water, space and other resources, given prevailing conditions. It is not a fixed universal number: habitat quality, climate, resource use and interactions among organisms can change it.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Biology, Organisms and Populations.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Biology, Organisms and Populations

questions.topic: Ecological niche — role of a species
questions.q: Which statement best distinguishes an ecological niche from a habitat?
o: A niche is the physical address only; a habitat is the species' feeding role
A niche describes a species' functional role and resource use; a habitat is the place where it lives
A niche applies only to plants; a habitat applies only to animals
The two terms always mean exactly the same thing
questions.e: A habitat is the place or environment in which an organism lives. Its ecological niche describes how it uses resources, interacts with other organisms and performs its functional role in the ecosystem. Several species may share a habitat while occupying different niches, reducing direct competition.
tags: Ecological niche — role of a species
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Biology, Organisms and Populations.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Biology, Organisms and Populations

questions.q: The ozone layer that absorbs much of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet-B radiation is concentrated in which atmospheric layer?
questions.e: The ozone layer is a region of relatively high ozone concentration in the stratosphere, roughly 15–35 km above Earth's surface. It absorbs much of the incoming UV-B radiation and acts as a protective shield for living organisms. Ground-level ozone, by contrast, is an air pollutant.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. UNEP Ozone Secretariat — Ozone and You.
questions.sourceName: UNEP Ozone Secretariat — Ozone and You

questions.q: A project plants selected grasses and trees on contaminated land so that pollutants are taken up, stabilised or helped to break down. This approach is called:
questions.e: Phytoremediation uses plants and associated root-zone processes to remove, contain or transform contaminants in soil, sediment or water. Depending on the contaminant and plant species, the process may involve uptake, stabilisation or support for microbial breakdown. It is a site-specific remediation method, not a universal substitute for every cleanup technology.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. US Environmental Protection Agency — Phytoremediation Technology Primer.
questions.sourceName: US Environmental Protection Agency — Phytoremediation Technology Primer

questions.q: Ground-level ozone in photochemical smog is classified as a secondary pollutant because it is:
o: Emitted directly from vehicle exhaust in the same form
Formed in the atmosphere through reactions involving precursor pollutants and sunlight
Released only from the upper stratosphere
questions.e: Ground-level ozone is not usually emitted directly. It forms in the atmosphere when nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds react in sunlight. This makes it a secondary pollutant. Ozone high in the stratosphere is beneficial because it absorbs ultraviolet radiation, but near the ground it can harm health and vegetation.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. US Environmental Protection Agency — Ground-Level Ozone Basics.
questions.sourceName: US Environmental Protection Agency — Ground-Level Ozone Basics

questions.q: For a renewable fish stock, sustainable yield is best understood as the harvest level that:
o: Always removes the entire annual population increase
Can be maintained over time without causing long-term depletion of the stock
Is fixed at the highest catch ever recorded
Does not depend on recruitment or natural mortality
questions.e: A sustainable yield is a harvest that can be maintained over time without undermining the resource's ability to regenerate. For fisheries, managers must consider recruitment, growth, natural mortality and uncertainty. A catch that exceeds replenishment for long periods can reduce the stock even if it produces a large short-term harvest.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. FAO — Fisheries and Aquaculture resources.
questions.sourceName: FAO — Fisheries and Aquaculture resources

questions.q: Four officers A, B, C and D sit at the four sides of a square table, all facing the centre. C sits opposite A, and B sits immediately clockwise from A. Who sits opposite B?
questions.e: With four seats, A and C occupy opposite positions. B is immediately clockwise from A, so the only remaining seat is occupied by D. That seat is opposite B. The condition that everyone faces the centre fixes the meaning of clockwise and avoids the ambiguity that occurs when people face outward.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Original authoring — independent circular-arrangement reasoning problem.
questions.sourceName: Original authoring — independent circular-arrangement reasoning problem

questions.q: Mira is the sister of Nikhil. Nikhil is the father of Ria. How is Mira related to Ria?
questions.e: Nikhil is Ria's father, so Nikhil's sister Mira is Ria's paternal aunt. 'Paternal' refers to the father's side of the family, while 'maternal' refers to the mother's side. The relationship is determined by tracing the two stated links rather than assuming Mira's age or marital status.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Original authoring — independent family-relation reasoning problem.
questions.sourceName: Original authoring — independent family-relation reasoning problem

questions.q: Four files P, Q, R and S are placed on shelves numbered 1 to 4 from bottom to top. Q is immediately above P, R is above Q, and S is above R. Which file must be on shelf 3?
questions.e: The conditions establish the strict order P below Q below R below S. Because there are exactly four shelves and four files, the only possible arrangement from bottom to top is P, Q, R, S. Therefore R must occupy shelf 3. The immediate-adjacency condition between P and Q is consistent with this unique order.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Original authoring — independent constraint-ordering reasoning problem.
questions.sourceName: Original authoring — independent constraint-ordering reasoning problem

questions.q: A department claims that a new training module reduces data-entry errors. Which evidence would most strongly strengthen the claim?
o: Errors fell only in the month when fewer files were processed
A comparable group not given the module had no similar fall, while trained staff showed a measured reduction
The training module received positive comments from its designer
The department changed its stationery during the same period
questions.e: A comparison group helps isolate the effect of the training from other influences. If trained staff show a reduction while a comparable untrained group does not, the evidence is more consistent with the module causing the improvement. Positive comments or unrelated changes do not establish the causal link.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Original authoring — independent critical-reasoning problem.
questions.sourceName: Original authoring — independent critical-reasoning problem

questions.topic: Critical reasoning — weaken a causal claim
questions.q: A manager says that a new attendance system caused late arrivals to fall. Which fact most weakens the conclusion?
o: The system records arrival time electronically
The same period included a transport strike ending, which independently made commuting easier
Employees were informed about the new system
The system produces a monthly report
questions.e: The end of a transport strike is an alternative explanation for fewer late arrivals. Because commuting became easier at the same time, the reduction cannot confidently be attributed to the attendance system alone. A good causal assessment looks for confounding factors and, where possible, compares similar groups or periods.
tags: Critical reasoning — weaken a causal claim
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Original authoring — independent critical-reasoning problem.
questions.sourceName: Original authoring — independent critical-reasoning problem

questions.q: An office proposes online appointments on the ground that they will shorten queues. Which assumption is necessary for this argument to work?
o: The appointment system will spread arrivals more evenly without reducing the office's ability to serve applicants
No applicant will ever arrive late
All services require exactly the same processing time
questions.e: The proposal can shorten queues only if appointments distribute demand in a useful way and the office retains enough capacity to process applicants. Smartphone ownership or identical service times are not necessary assumptions; access can be provided through other channels and services may vary in length.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Original authoring — independent critical-reasoning problem.
questions.sourceName: Original authoring — independent critical-reasoning problem

questions.q: A permit is issued only if the prescribed fee has been paid. If a permit has been issued, which conclusion must be true?
questions.e: 'A only if B' means B is a necessary condition for A. Therefore, if the permit (A) has been issued, the fee-payment condition (B) must have been satisfied. The statement does not establish that payment alone guarantees a permit; it says only that payment is necessary.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Original authoring — independent conditional-reasoning problem.
questions.sourceName: Original authoring — independent conditional-reasoning problem

questions.q: Three rooms are assigned one each to Audit, Records and Accounts. Audit is not in Room 1. Records is in a higher-numbered room than Audit. Accounts is not in Room 3. Which room must contain Records?
questions.e: Audit cannot be in Room 1. If Audit were in Room 3, no room would be higher for Records, so Audit must be in Room 1 or 2. But Accounts cannot be in Room 3, and each room is used once. The only arrangement satisfying all conditions is Audit in Room 1, Accounts in Room 2 and Records in Room 3.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Original authoring — independent constraint-satisfaction reasoning problem.
questions.sourceName: Original authoring — independent constraint-satisfaction reasoning problem

questions.q: A report states that complaint numbers fell after a new online grievance portal was launched, proving that public services improved. Which observation most directly challenges the conclusion?
o: The portal uses a modern colour scheme
The portal was unavailable for several weeks, and complaints could not be submitted during that period
The report was printed on recycled paper
The department held a staff meeting after launch
questions.e: If the portal was unavailable, fewer complaints may have been recorded simply because people could not submit them. The fall in recorded complaints would then not demonstrate better service. This is a measurement problem: the number of complaints received is not necessarily the same as the number of problems experienced.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Original authoring — independent critical-reasoning problem.
questions.sourceName: Original authoring — independent critical-reasoning problem

questions.q: In the OSI reference model, which layer is primarily responsible for logical addressing and routing packets between networks?
questions.e: The Network layer is Layer 3 of the OSI model. It handles logical addressing and routing so packets can travel across interconnected networks. The Data Link layer handles delivery on a local link, while the Transport layer provides end-to-end transport services between communicating hosts.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. ITU-T Recommendation X.200 — Open Systems Interconnection reference model.
questions.sourceName: ITU-T Recommendation X.200 — Open Systems Interconnection reference model

questions.q: What is the primary function of the Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) on an IP network?
o: Encrypting files stored on a server
Automatically supplying network configuration such as IP addresses to clients
Converting domain names into IP addresses
Transferring outgoing email between mail servers
questions.e: DHCP allows a networked client to obtain configuration parameters automatically, commonly including an IP address, subnet information, default gateway and DNS server information. This reduces manual configuration and helps manage address allocation. DNS name resolution and SMTP email transfer are separate services.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. IETF — RFC 2131, Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol.
questions.sourceName: IETF — RFC 2131, Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes a cryptographic hash from ordinary encryption?
o: A hash is designed as a one-way digest, while encryption is designed to be reversible with the appropriate key
A hash always requires a public and private key pair
A hash is simply a compressed copy that can always be restored
questions.e: A cryptographic hash function maps input data to a fixed-length digest and is designed to be computationally infeasible to reverse. Encryption transforms data so that an authorised holder of the appropriate key can recover the plaintext. Hashing is commonly used for integrity checks, while encryption protects confidentiality.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NIST — Secure Hash Standard, FIPS 180-4.
questions.sourceName: NIST — Secure Hash Standard, FIPS 180-4

questions.q: Which combination is a genuine example of multi-factor authentication?
o: Password plus a memorable security question
questions.e: Multi-factor authentication uses factors from different categories: something the user knows, has or is. A password is a knowledge factor and a fingerprint is an inherence factor, so the combination uses two distinct categories. Two passwords or a password plus a security question are both knowledge factors.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NIST — Digital Identity Guidelines, Authentication and Lifecycle Management.
questions.sourceName: NIST — Digital Identity Guidelines, Authentication and Lifecycle Management

questions.q: Which protocol is primarily used to submit and transfer outgoing email between mail clients and mail servers or between mail servers?
questions.e: SMTP, the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol, is used to send or relay email. IMAP and POP3 are primarily used by clients to access or retrieve messages from mailboxes, while SNMP is used for network management. The direction and purpose of the protocol are the key distinctions.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. IETF — RFC 5321, Simple Mail Transfer Protocol.
questions.sourceName: IETF — RFC 5321, Simple Mail Transfer Protocol

questions.q: A database table has no single column that uniquely identifies each row, but the combination of EmployeeID and TrainingID is unique. What should the table use?
questions.e: A composite primary key consists of two or more columns whose combined values uniquely identify each row. Here, EmployeeID alone may repeat because an employee can attend several courses, and TrainingID alone may repeat because many employees attend one course. Their combination identifies each employee-training record.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. PostgreSQL Documentation — Constraints and Primary Keys.
questions.sourceName: PostgreSQL Documentation — Constraints and Primary Keys

questions.q: In a spreadsheet, conditional formatting is used primarily to:
o: Change a cell's appearance automatically when a specified rule is met
Encrypt the workbook with a public key
Convert every formula into a static value
questions.e: Conditional formatting applies visual formats such as colour, icons or data bars when cell values satisfy specified rules. It helps users identify patterns and exceptions without changing the underlying cell value. It is different from data validation, which controls what users may enter.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Microsoft Support — Excel conditional formatting.
questions.sourceName: Microsoft Support — Excel conditional formatting

questions.q: A user accesses a complete accounting application through a web browser while the provider manages the servers, operating system and application. Which cloud service model is this?
questions.e: Software as a Service (SaaS) delivers a complete application to users over a network. The provider manages the underlying infrastructure and application platform, while the customer mainly configures and uses the software. IaaS supplies computing infrastructure and PaaS supplies a platform for deploying applications.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NIST — The NIST Definition of Cloud Computing, SP 800-145.

questions.q: The sum of the interior angles of a polygon is 2,340°. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.e: For an n-sided polygon, the sum of interior angles is (n−2) × 180°. Thus (n−2) × 180 = 2,340, so n−2 = 13 and n = 15. The calculation uses the fact that a convex polygon can be divided into n−2 triangles from one vertex.

questions.q: A router allows several devices using private IP addresses to access the internet through one public IP address by rewriting address information in packets. Which technique is being used?
questions.e: Network Address Translation rewrites IP address information as packets pass between networks, commonly allowing multiple private-network devices to share a public address. Port Address Translation can distinguish simultaneous connections by using transport-layer port numbers. DHCP assigns network configuration; it does not perform address translation.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes lossless data compression?
o: The original data can be reconstructed exactly after decompression
Some original information is permanently discarded
It can be used only for audio files
It automatically encrypts the compressed file
questions.e: Lossless compression reduces the amount of data needed to represent information while preserving enough information to reconstruct the original data exactly. It is useful for text, program files and image formats such as PNG, where even a small change may matter. Lossy compression achieves higher reduction by discarding information that may be less noticeable.

questions.q: Under Article 267(1), the Contingency Fund of India is placed at the disposal of whom so that advances can be made for unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by Parliament?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.e: Article 267(1) provides for a Contingency Fund of India in the nature of an imprest. It is placed at the disposal of the President to enable advances for meeting unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by Parliament by law. Article 267(2) separately allows a State Legislature to establish a State Contingency Fund placed at the disposal of the Governor.
